job.style: a description of a classroom activity or experiment and what it shows

passage: In our Social Science class today, we conducted a simulation to understand the role of government in ensuring social justice. We imagined a town where a private company controlled all water supplies and set prices based on profit margins. We quickly realized that families who could not afford the high costs were left without clean water, proving that water is a fundamental right that must be accessible to everyone, not just a commodity for those who can pay. We then discussed the Bhopal Gas Tragedy, analyzing how it was not merely an unfortunate accident, but a result of the company’s decision to ignore safety protocols to cut costs. This highlighted why strict government regulations are essential to protect citizens from corporate negligence. Finally, we examined labor laws. We learned that minimum wage laws are vital because they prevent the exploitation of workers, ensuring that employers cannot pay unfairly low wages regardless of their desire for higher profits. These laws act as a necessary shield for the vulnerable, ensuring that economic growth does not come at the expense of basic human dignity or safety. Through these activities, we concluded that the government must intervene in the market to uphold justice and protect the rights of all citizens.

items.evidence: We imagined a town where a private company controlled all water supplies and set prices based on profit margins.
items.q: In the simulated town, why did some families have no clean water?
options: Prices were set to earn profit, so they could not pay
The company ran out of water for the town
The government gave water only to rich areas
Families chose not to use the company's supply
items.explain: The company set prices by profit, so families who could not afford them were left without clean water.

wrong.why: thinks a supply means enough water for everyone
blames the government instead of the company
thinks families chose to go without

items.evidence: We quickly realized that families who could not afford the high costs were left without clean water, proving that water is a fundamental right that must be accessible to everyone, not just a commodity for those who can pay.
items.q: A student says only people who can pay should get water. Which reply fits the lesson?
options: Water is a basic right, so all must reach it
Water is a product, so sellers should decide
Water is free, so nobody can be charged
Water is a right only for poor families
items.explain: Water is a fundamental right that must be accessible to everyone, not just to those who can pay.

wrong.why: thinks water is a commodity for payers only
thinks a right to water means it must be free
thinks public facilities are only for poor people

items.evidence: We then discussed the Bhopal Gas Tragedy, analyzing how it was not merely an unfortunate accident, but a result of the company’s decision to ignore safety protocols to cut costs.
items.q: Why does the passage say the Bhopal Gas Tragedy was not just bad luck?
options: The company chose to skip safety steps to save money
The workers did not look after their own safety
The company paid a small sum and ended its duty
The government had stopped all rules for factories
items.explain: The company decided to ignore safety protocols to cut costs, so the harm came from a choice, not chance.

wrong.why: thinks safety is the worker's own job
blames missing rules instead of the company's decision

items.evidence: This highlighted why strict government regulations are essential to protect citizens from corporate negligence.
items.q: A factory could save money by ignoring safety. What does strict regulation do here?
options: It forces the owner to protect people first
It lets the owner decide what is safe
It leaves safety to each worker's care
It makes the factory pay less for harm
items.explain: Strict government regulations protect citizens from corporate negligence, so owners cannot put saving money above safety.

wrong.why: thinks regulation leaves safety to the company
thinks safety is the worker's own responsibility
thinks paying a little ends responsibility for harm

items.evidence: We learned that minimum wage laws are vital because they prevent the exploitation of workers, ensuring that employers cannot pay unfairly low wages regardless of their desire for higher profits.
items.q: Why are minimum wage laws needed, even when employers want higher profits?
options: They stop employers from paying unfairly low wages
They let employers set pay as they wish
They protect only workers who are in factories
They help the company earn more profit
items.explain: Minimum wage laws prevent exploitation by stopping employers from paying unfairly low wages, whatever their profit wishes.

wrong.why: thinks employers should pay whatever they want
thinks labour laws protect only factory workers
reverses the purpose of the law
